message:
A pair at midspan beats spreading units along the span for this bridge, Bridge Retrofit Engineer. In plain words both masses at the antinode give full push per kilogram while units moved off centre do less work. At the edge of the middle third the mode shape is 0.866 and the mass effectiveness is 0.750 from the modal-effectiveness calculation (E67), so a spread layout needs about one third more moving mass for the same damping.

The hanger depth is set by sag plus shake, not shake alone. In plain words the soft spring stretches under its own weight more than it moves in vibration and that total drop sizes the cage. Static sag 74.7 mm from the static-sag calculation (E63) plus peak travel 49.4 mm from the free-decay simulation (E17) sums to 124 mm total from the envelope calculation (E68), about a hand length and well below a door width, which fits inside girder depth as shown in the twin under-deck layout sketch (E55).

Your friction rule makes from-below install buildable, Bridge Retrofit Engineer. I take from the 1 Experiments on coldformed steel momentresisting connections with 2 bolting frictionslip mechanism (E57) that slip capacity is calculated per EN 1993-1-8 with friction coefficient 0.3, which confirms from my discipline that the High-Strength Friction-Grip, defined as High-Strength Friction-Grip (HSFG), clamped cross-beam for the Tuned Mass Damper, defined as Tuned Mass Damper (TMD), can be fitted from below with ordinary tools and no weld or drill. One bolt gives 32.9 kN slip resistance from the slip-resistance calculation (E64) against 13.1 kN combined demand from the combined-load calculation (E65), about eighteen body weights, so four bolts give redundancy against loosening at 1.9 Hz.

My position is not ready, because the access route and stop impact into the cross-beam still need agreement.
